parent_claim: HapRepair should be more reliable than a coding-agent-only baseline under matched inputs, model, analyzer feedback, and evaluator gates.
comparison_baselines: coding-agent-only baseline under the matched v6 protocol

slices.reviewer_question: Is the apparent advantage stable across clean repetitions and all 35 projects?
slices.fixed_conditions: Same frozen inputs, model, localization, five-scan budget, six-turn active-round allowance, and evaluator gates.
slices.claim_update: The final-alert direction favors HapRepair in both repetitions (20.800 and 17.971 fewer alerts per project).
slices.comparability: direct and intention-to-treat; cluster by project
slices.next_action: Report both repetition effects and clustered uncertainty.

slices.reviewer_question: Does HapRepair's benefit increase with the frozen initial alert burden?
slices.fixed_conditions: Outcome-independent 12/11/12 strata and continuous log1p burden model with project clustering.
slices.claim_update: The log-burden slope is -0.672 (p=0.8262); retain this as a descriptive interaction.

slices.reviewer_question: Are condition gaps caused by repair behavior or by provider/infrastructure accidents?
slices.fixed_conditions: All conditions use the same inputs, model, analyzer feedback, budgets, and evaluator gates; method failures remain in the denominator.
slices.claim_update: All 70 Skill conditions completed; the 12 remaining failures belong to the baseline.
slices.comparability: Direct under matched inputs, model, budgets, and evaluator gates.

evaluation_summary.takeaway: HapRepair produced an evaluator-acceptable candidate for all 70 project-repetition conditions and left fewer alerts than the fixed baseline in both repetitions.

stop_condition: Met with all canonical results complete.
next_action: Reconcile the narrowed claims into the outline, then revise the manuscript and response letter without launching additional repair experiments.
